summary: Explicit imbalance handling (class weighting or SMOTE) gives at most a small F1-macro improvement over baseline models on this dataset (+0.0011 for the best config vs best unweighted baseline, 5-fold CV). Random Forest with class weighting/SMOTE modestly raises minority-class recall relative to baseline, but ROC-AUC and PR-AUC (ranking quality) are essentially unchanged, and the F1-macro gain is small relative to fold-to-fold noise.
primary_metric_name: F1-macro difference (best imbalance-handled - best baseline), 5-fold CV
direction: negligible difference: imbalance handling does not meaningfully change F1-macro
methodological_choices: Target encoded as binary (>50K=1). Missing categorical values (workclass, occupation, native-country) kept as an explicit 'Missing' category rather than imputed or dropped. Numeric features standardized; categoricals one-hot encoded inside a ColumnTransformer. Two model families compared: Logistic Regression (max_iter=2000) and Random Forest (300 trees). Three imbalance-handling strategies per model: none (baseline), class_weight='balanced', and SMOTE oversampling (applied only within training folds via an imblearn Pipeline to avoid leakage). Primary comparison via 5-fold stratified CV on a 70% training split; a held-out 30% test set used only as a confirmatory single-split check. Primary metric chosen as F1-macro (threshold-dependent, treats both classes equally) rather than ROC-AUC/PR-AUC, since imbalance techniques mainly shift the decision threshold/class weighting rather than ranking quality, and ROC-AUC is largely insensitive to that.
verification_method: 5x repeated 5-fold stratified CV (25 folds total, seed=123) on the full dataset for Random Forest baseline vs class_weight vs SMOTE, comparing mean +/- std of F1-macro against the primary train-split CV result.
verification_result: Held up in direction: RF baseline F1-macro = 0.7897 +/- 0.0038 vs best imbalance-handled (class_weight) = 0.7928 +/- 0.0039 (delta +0.0031). The gain is small and on the order of, or smaller than, the fold-to-fold standard deviation, confirming the primary finding that imbalance handling produces at most a small, largely threshold/recall-related improvement rather than a substantial gain in overall model quality.
